title: Salman Khan Wants to Play a Warrior King — and He's Picked Rang De Basanti's Director to Do It
excerpt: A two-part period epic with Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra and Farhan Akhtar's Excel Entertainment is in advanced talks. Salman would play 'one of the most revered figures from Indian history' — and reshape his body to do it.
body:
Some scoops you can feel the ambition radiating off. This is one of them.

Salman Khan — the most stubbornly larger-than-life star Bollywood has, the man who has spent three decades selling sheer presence — is in advanced talks to do something he has never quite done: disappear into a role. According to a Bollywood Hungama report, Salman is close to signing a two-part period epic to be directed by Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra, the National Award-winning filmmaker behind Rang De Basanti and Bhaag Milkha Bhaag, and produced by Farhan Akhtar and Ritesh Sidhwani's Excel Entertainment.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=F3DIf3nwbFc

Read that lineup again, because it's the kind of pairing that sounds almost too neat to be real. Salman, all instinct and swagger. Mehra, all texture and conscience. Excel, the prestige house that turned Dil Chahta Hai and Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara into generational touchstones. If this comes together, it's the first time any of them has worked with the others — Salman has never made a film with Mehra, and never with Akhtar's banner. Three reputations, none of them overlapping, all betting on the same script.

https://x.com/TradeBOC/status/2069436324369805397

And what a part it apparently is. Sources say Salman will play 'one of the most popular and revered figures from Indian history' — a warrior from the past — and that he was 'bowled over' by the character after hearing the narration.

"Salman is looking to sign on for big projects and believes that the Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra film will do justice to his larger-than-life aura. He will be playing one of the most popular characters from Indian History and will undergo a complete makeover of his body structure." — Source to Bollywood Hungama

That last line is the one that should make fans sit up. A 'complete makeover of his body structure' is not the language of a Salman vehicle, where the abs arrive in slow motion and the plot bends around them. It's the language of transformation — of an actor who has watched Prabhas, Ranbir Kapoor, and an entire generation of pan-India epics raise the spectacle bar, and decided he wants in on the serious version. At a moment when the period saga is the most prestige-laden, biggest-grossing genre in Indian cinema, Salman planting his flag here is a statement of intent.

The timing is pure strategy. Salman is, by every account, building an aggressive theatrical pipeline. He's currently wrapping an action entertainer with director Vamshi Paidipally, and is set to begin a superhero comedy with the Raj & DK duo around October 2026. The Mehra epic would roll only after that — production is pencilled for summer 2027 — which means the dotted line isn't signed yet. Discussions are reportedly still circling the usual pressure points: shooting days and remuneration, the two things that have derailed more Salman projects than any script ever could.

Still, the enthusiasm sounds genuine. Khan and Akhtar have apparently been meeting regularly over the past month to map the vision, and insiders describe it as a passion project for everyone in the room. That tracks. Mehra doesn't make disposable films — Rang De Basanti still detonates on rewatch, and Bhaag Milkha Bhaag remains one of the great Hindi sports dramas. His one stumble, the Farhan Akhtar boxing drama Toofaan, was the exception that proved he works best with weight and history, not montage. A warrior epic is squarely his terrain.

For the diaspora, the appeal writes itself. Period spectacle is the genre that travels furthest — Baahubali, RRR, Padmaavat all found enormous overseas audiences, dubbed and subtitled into every market with a desi multiplex. A Salman Khan historical, mounted on this scale and split across two parts, is precisely the sort of event NRIs in the US, UK, and Canada turn into opening-weekend pilgrimages. Two films means two such weekends.

Nothing is locked. Salman, the report notes, needs his time before making 'an informed decision,' and more clarity is expected only toward the end of the year. But the very fact that he's chasing a director this prestigious, for a role that demands he remake his body and submit to a vision bigger than his own brand, is the most interesting thing the actor has signalled in years.

The boy from Bandra wants to play a king. And for once, he's willing to do the work to earn the crown.
